content:
CONFIRMED

- `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\applications\ji-host-core\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\host\HostStorePersistence.java:17-19` defines `timeline(...)` as a default method throwing `UnsupportedOperationException`. Existing/custom implementations therefore remain source-compatible without implementing it.
- `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\applications\ji-host-core\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\host\PersistentHostStore.java:198-200` delegates directly to `persistence.timeline(...)`, without capability detection or error translation.
- `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\applications\ji-host-web\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\host\web\LocalHostServer.java:252-254,269-275` invokes that path for the timeline endpoint.
- `LocalHostServer.java:853-871` catches `JiException`, artifact/Jackson failures, `IllegalArgumentException`, and `IllegalStateException`, but not `UnsupportedOperationException` or general `RuntimeException`. Thus the default exception escapes the handler rather than producing `application/problem+json`, potentially terminating the HTTP exchange/connection.
- The built-in SQLite adapter overrides `timeline(...)`, but `ji-host-core` does not depend on SQLite, so external/custom persistence implementations can compile while retaining this runtime failure.
